chapters.html:
Aedes Elysiae is generally a peaceful place, though perhaps idyllic might be the more accurate term. After all, nothing really happens to the village, and the villagers often joke that they've been forgotten by everyone, even the Titans.

But of course, humans will always find a way to invent something that lurks in the night.

Beware the beast in the woods. Jaws that can fit a grown man between them with ease, footsteps that shake the earth, and claws that easily rend apart even the strongest shields like it’s paper.

For as long as Phainon can remember, The Beast had always been this nebulous, fearsome creature that remains on the dark edges of memory. Sure, he believed it the first few times that his mother told him about it, swearing that she'd seen grooves in the wood that couldn't have been made by anyone other than it, but like anyone else, he grew up.

He stops listening to fairytales, stops believing in his childhood, and instead busies himself with helping his mother and father out on the farm.

Then, his father disappears.

Galba had returned from a hunting expedition, dishevelled, missing his bow and babbling about a castle in the woods. It'd taken the better part of the day to coax him down to some semblance of calm, and even then, he'd only started talking when Audata started crying, begging to know where her husband went.

"M-monster," Galba stammers, his eyes wild. "It was huge, enormous. Hieronymus pushed me away, told me to– to go. He said he would be right behind me."

Galba's voice breaks, and he buries his face in his hands.

"Hieronymus…" Audata's face hardens, and she rises to her feet. "He's not dead. I know he's not dead, he's out there somewhere."

"Mother, please." Phainon tries to pull her down, to console her, but she rips herself away from his hands.

"Phainon, know this. If that beast in the woods truly killed my husband, I won't stop until I've either joined him, or brought him down."

In the end, he does manage to coax down his mother, saying that she would be better off waiting for the morning to come before making such a decision. A few strong servings of soothing tea later, and Audata is curled up in her bed, her figure somehow frail and thin under the blankets.

Between his mother and him, Phainon stands a better chance against the beast. Still, as he checks his small knapsack, he laments the fact that Aedes Elysiae is a farming village. The only weapon that he has is a hoe, its usually dull edge sharpened to a razor gleam, as well as the knife that he uses to shape wooden figurines.

He packs very little food and water, reasoning that he can forage just enough for himself, and just as he's rising to leave the village, he hears a rustle outside.

"Heading out for a late night walk, Phainon?"

Quietly, he curses under his breath. Of course she would realise. Cyrene had always been way too perceptive.

"Just a stroll to get some fresh air, you know," he says, turning around to face her.

Cyrene hums, then quick as a flash, darts forward and pulls the knapsack into view. He groans, but she just giggles.

"Why, Phainon, I didn't know a late night walk needed you to bring a sharpened hoe and food!" Cyrene's smile is sharp. "Now, let's try this again."

"I have to," Phainon says quietly. "I can't let my mother grieve like that, Cyrene, I can't."

"What if you die?" She drops the bag, and it swings back against his back. So light, but somehow, it feels like the weight of the world rests on his back.

"I won't."

"Can you promise that? Swear it upon Tantalon's scales, and they won't tilt?"

"No, but I have a failsafe." From his pocket, he draws out a letter and hands it to Cyrene. "I need you to pretend that you found this on my bed in the morning."

"You're kidding." She turns the note over in her hands. "What does this say?"

"I left to find help at Castrum Kremnos, so that she won't have to worry, that sort of thing." Phainon shrugs, backing away from her. "You'll help me, right?"

"I hate the way you think, sometimes." Cyrene sighs, but she tucks the letter into her pocket. "Live well, Phainon."

"Live long, Cyrene." Phainon grins. "See you after I've slayed a beast."

That's what he says, but half a day later, the sun is shining down on his head and he's no closer to tracking down this beast. If the legends are to be believed, then even a blind man could've located this beast. But somehow, there is no fur, no loose teeth, not even a footprint for him to get clues from.

And there's the matter of the forest. From his map, he should've walked out of the forest twice over now. But here he is, standing in the middle of the woods, completely and utterly lost.

At this rate, he'll die of starvation before he even finds the supposed castle.

"Ugh." He rolls up the map and stuffs it into his bag, then closes his eyes and spins around twice. When he opens them, he starts marching in that direction.

The birdsong goes silent for a moment, as though even the forest were shocked by his audacious attitude, but Phainon's confident enough in his abilities and desperate enough to try anything.

He walks and walks, even as the sun sets and casts long shadows through the gaps between the trees. Even as the birds fall silent in favour of grasshoppers and crickets, he forgets on, using his hoe to chop away at the vegetation that seems to be curling around his legs at any chance.

As if to make everything worse, rain begins to fall, soaking him to the bone and probably ruining the last of his rations.

"Great! Just great!" Phainon yells out loud and immediately gets a mouthful of water for his troubles. He continues to grumble as he stomps through the wet foliage, slapping away stray branches.

"Stupid rain, stupid forest…stupid beast who probably doesn't own a palace…" Moodily, he kicks at the ground under him, and his boot knocks against something hard.

He pauses.

It's far too dark to see anything, so he drops to his feet and starts brushing away the rotting wet leaves, feeling out the shape of what he'd kicked.

They're semi-regular, each one about the size of his torso and placed about two fingers length away from each other. The gaps between are packed with wet gravel, and the answer makes itself clear moments later.

Flagstones.

This is a path.

Excitedly, he scrambles to his feet and looks up.

A shape solidifies from out of the fog. Tall, impressive looking spires, spiked with dark metal. The walls of the mansion are dark with rainwater and moss, and there's a general air of desolation around it.

But to Phainon, it's like he's hit the jackpot.

He hurries to the walls, checking over it until he spots a small area where it's collapsed inwards. With a bit of wriggling, he manages to get into the inner grounds, which are as overgrown as the outside.

From there, it's a short run to the walls of the palace, which are surprisingly well-kept for a supposedly abandoned place. At least, that's what he assumes from the exterior.

The interior is lavish, almost disgustingly so. Dark marbled floors that look so expensive he feels guilty for dripping water onto them, delicate looking vases and sideboards, and a warmth that permeates the entire place like a warm bath.

Maybe the beast is more used to a tropical climate? He wonders as he looks around for a way down into a basement. Every place like this always has a basement, and he's proven right when he spots a stone staircase leading down into the darkness.

His matches are all waterlogged, but thankfully he finds a candle on the verge of drowning itself and rescues it, pinching its wick out from the wax. With that single meagre light source by his side, he makes his way down into the depths.

By the flickering light of the candle, he can see bars, set into brick walls, and his heart plummets. This is a dungeon. Thankfully, there doesn't seem to be anyone in the cells that he passes, and with each empty cell, his hopes grow dimmer and dimmer until he reaches the very last one.

In there, he can almost see a vague outline of darkness curled up in a corner, and hope comes back in such force that it dizzies him.

"Dad? Dad, are you there?" Phainon whispers, setting the candle down and peering into the cell. It's clear that this cell is occupied, but he can't tell if it's his father or just another unfortunate poor soul, caught by the beast.

A thought festers within him, though. What if that body in there…what if his father is…

"Your father is still alive."

Phainon whips around, and the air leaves his lungs in a whoosh as he realises just what is standing before him.

The beast is huge. A mane of thick, red hair frames its distinctly feline face, and golden eyes stare out from the face. Its teeth are long, almost as long as Phainon's arm, and even crouched down to fit in the dungeons, it still towers a full head and shoulders above him.

And somehow, it had managed to sneak up on him.

"Trespasser," it rumbles. "Why have you come?"

"You've kidnapped my father." Phainon stands, gripping his hoe tightly. "Let him go."

"He trespassed as well. Am I not allowed to deal with intruders as I see fit?" A grin reveals every tooth in its mouth, and it chuckles. "Or am I to let you all make fools of me?"

"If you don't let him go, I'll kill you."

At that, the beast really does laugh, tipping its head back and making a sound that resembles an animal's roar rather than laughter.

"With that tiny thing in your hands?" The monster jabs a claw at his hoe. "Little human, spare yourself the pain. I shall offer you a trade."

"A trade?" Phainon remains suspicious, but hope rises in his chest. Perhaps this thing has intelligence. And if it is intelligent, then it can be tricked. It can be bargained with.

"Your life for your father's. Stay here, and in exchange, your father will go free."

His answer is immediate.

"Deal. But you have to make sure he makes it back to my village safely."

"I wouldn't know which village you came from unless you told me."

A small, childish part of Phainon wants to rebel against giving out the name of his village to this thing, but the larger part of him would put his head between the beast's jaws if it meant his father would return home safely.

"Aedes Elysiae."

"Understood." It shifts, and Phainon can see muscle rippling under the fur. He grips his weapon tightly as the beast strides past him, pushing a claw into the lock and twisting it sharply. With a screech, the door opens, and Phainon rushes in.

His father looks healthy, if a little gaunt. His lips are pale, and he's feverishly hot. Had he fallen ill in the dungeon somehow? Carefully, he gathers Hieronymus' limbs together before lifting his father, carrying him over to the beast.

"Keep your promise."

"Do you take me for a wild beast?" It snarls, and Phainon stares disbelievingly at it.

"Do I– have you looked in a mirror?"

"I should rip your tongue out. Perhaps then you might learn how well silence serves you."

The beast turns on his heel and storms out of the dungeon. Phainon tries to follow, he really does, but the adrenaline leaves him all at once. His legs give out from under him, and he wheezes, clutching at his chest.

Eventually, he does recover enough to get out of the dungeon, even if he has to brace himself against the wall the entire time.

It's only when he makes it to the landing does he realise that the beast…hadn't actually told him anything about the palace. He doesn't even know where the bedrooms are, let alone a bathroom where he can take a long hot bath and get the smell of rain and mud out of his skin.

"Hello!"

He blinks. Maybe he's really losing it, if he's starting to hear the voice of a child in a place like this. There's a loud click, and then something bumps against his feet.

When he looks down, a doll is staring up at him, its eyes blinking sweetly at him.

"Oh," he says faintly. "I'm going crazy. The furniture is starting to talk to me now."

"We're not furniture!" The doll bounces around, and then it splits into two, its top popping off to reveal smaller, slightly different versions of itself that hop out and crowd around him. "We are Tribbie!"

"All…" He does a quick headcount. "Four of you?"

"Yes!" One of the smaller ones chirps. "But together, we are Tribios! Are you a new visitor?"

"Sort of. Are you…humans?"

"What a funny question!" Tribbie laughs. "No, of course not! We're dolls!"

As if to demonstrate, all of the tiny versions hop back into the larger doll, which snaps shut. Phainon blinks.

"You look tired. But don't worry, we can help! Follow us!"

The doll bounces ahead without even looking back to see if Phainon is following them. He weighs the pros and cons of following a potentially creepy doll through the halls of the beast's palace, and decides that if he really is going to die, he's going to get a hot meal and a bath first.

Tribbie takes him down a few turns, hopping along at a surprisingly fast pace. She only requires him to open the door to their destination, which is apparently a bedroom. A large, four-poster bed occupies most of the room, and outside the window, he can see the storm howling.

"Rest here for now!" Tribbie says. "There's a bath connected to the bedroom, and if you want food, pull that." She hops over to an ornate looking rope, the tassel thick and heavy.

"Thank you. Um…did the beast tell you to do this?"

"The beast? Oh, you mean De? No, he didn't. But we think that he would like for a guest to be treated well in his home!"

"…De?" Phainon repeats. "Is that his name?"

It just…seems a little incongruent with the enormous figure that he'd seen, that's all. No other reason.

"We call him De, but he has his own name." Tribbie sways from side to side before she hops back towards the door. "Sleep well, Snowy. See you tomorrow!"

He watches the doll hop out of the door, and the clicking sound soon fades away as the doll leaves for…wherever a doll goes to rest.

'De' was apparently a diminutive of his name, and the dolls, which seem no older than children, have a positive impression of him. Tribbie had seemed genuinely helpful, but he couldn't rule out the possibility of her working with the beast.

Carefully, he sets out to explore his surroundings. The bedroom doesn't seem to have any hidden corridors or trapdoors, and the bath seems like a perfectly normal bath, albeit a little big for just himself. The architecture of the room seems familiar somehow, but Phainon can't quite put his finger on it.

Eventually, the feeling of his clothes drying tackily against his skin is incentive enough for him to strip and get into the baths, and the water is so comfortable that he melts against the tiles, letting the heat work its magic.

Marching through the woods, making a deal with the beast from the legends, and talking dolls, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to say that it's been a long day for Phainon. After a long bath, he's feeling significantly calmer now, and he gets to work barricading the room against any intrusions. Luckily for him, there's just one door that he has to worry about, and he hauls the chest of drawers and the wardrobe against it, then tucks his knife into the folds of his sleep clothes for good measure.

It might not stop the monster entirely, but it would at least give him some time to react.

Entrance finally barricaded, he checks over the room one more time before collapsing onto the bed. Fear and fatigue battle it out in his body, and eventually, his mind succumbs to fatigue.

But not for long.

A crash startles him awake, and his fingers scrabble for his knife before he's even fully awake. It takes him a few moments to actually realise what had happened, and a chill goes down his spine when he realises his barricade had done its job.

The chest of drawers had fallen over, its drawers spilling out onto the floor. It speaks volumes of its make and quality that it's barely dented, but the door is ever so slightly ajar, and outside–

Phainon inhales sharply when he spots the glowing golden eye, floating in the darkness.

"So, it seems like you've made yourself quite the nest." The eye curves, and he can almost imagine the leering grin that comes with that. "Barricading yourself into one of my rooms?"

"You said I was a guest," Phainon shoots back. "Should I not be comfortable, then?"

"A guest does not block the host from letting themselves in. You are acting as though you're a prisoner."

He might as well be, he doesn't say, but it's a close thing. Reluctantly, he marches up to the wardrobe that he'd shoved against the door, tucking the blade into his pocket and grabbing the piece of furniture. He heaves, and the wardrobe crashes to the ground with a sound that rattles his bones. The door swings open, and Phainon barely has a chance to react before a hand closes around him.

"Do not test me." The beast snarls, its teeth inches away from his head. "I swore to bring your father back to your piddling little village, and you repay me by breaking my things?"

"How would I even know if you'd really sent my father back, or taken him away and eaten him somewhere that I can't see?" The grip around him is tightening, his ribs creaking under the strain, but he continues. "You're keeping me captive here, don't you forget that. If you want me to behave, then give me a reason to."

His vision is starting to go spotty, Phainon realises. Any more of this and he might genuinely crack a rib, but he's not going to give the beast the satisfaction of begging. The edges of his vision goes grey, and he's on the verge of passing out when the grip around his body releases, and he collapses onto the ground, hacking and wheezing. His entire body feels sore, and he glares up at the beast.

"You are a guest here," it says at last. "I cannot control your behaviour, even if you want to be unruly. For as long as you remain here, you are free to roam the premises. But do not enter the western spire. That is the one thing I ask of you."

"I…" Phainon wheezes. "I don't even know your name."

"Call me Deimos." The beast turns, ducking under the doorframe and heading out into the hallway. "It is the only name that you will get from me in this place."

Deimos, meaning fear, or the terror that strikes armies before a battle. A very apt name for a creature like him. Phainon watches as he leaves, noting that he wears a cloak on his back, the fabric almost indistinguishable from his ruddy fur. A long tail lashes behind, short fur tipped with a longer curl of paler, almost blond fur.

And he is huge. Phainon had already known this from their first meeting, but in the morning light, he can truly see how tall Deimos is, despite being mostly on all fours and hunched over.

Quickly, he hurries out of the wreckage of his room and follows Deimos, keeping a safe distance between the two of them. The beast moves surprisingly swift for someone of such large size, and Phainon has to lengthen his strides to match.

When the beast slows to pull the large doors open, he takes the chance to speak.

"My name is Phainon."

Deimos snorts.

"What do you expect me to do with that?"

"Nothing. But you gave me your name, so I should return the favour."

Deimos lumbers into the room, and Phainon realises that it's a dining room, dishes already set on the large table before them. Unsurprisingly, most of them are meat dishes, and there are large pitchers of a dark red liquid dotting the table at regular intervals.

"Do what you want." Deimos doesn't seem to care that Phainon is quite literally standing behind him with a knife, instead choosing to head to the table and pick out a few choice samples of meat. Dromas steak, whole legs of roasted cloudsheep, and even an entire roast chicken disappears into his jaws with such speed that watching it makes Phainon slightly ill.

Then, he finishes it off with a pitcher of that dark red liquid, and Phainon sniffs the air cautiously, expecting the smell of iron.

Instead, the air is sweetly scented, reminiscent of that one time a wandering merchant had sold Aedes Elysiae her entire stock of fruit for a ridiculous discount because they were about to go bad. Bright red and round, and when they were cracked open, revealed countless tiny pips.

"Pomegranate," he says dumbly. "You're drinking…pomegranate juice?"

"Did you think it was blood?" Deimos sets the now empty jug down. "Perhaps you ought not to subscribe to such stereotypes."

"Forgive me for thinking that a creature like you would drink pomegranate juice."

Deimos harrumphs, settling down on his haunches and beginning to lick at the fur on his paws (hands?). When it becomes clear that he's not leaving the room, Phainon creeps forward and looks over the spread of food on the table. In the end, he picks the bread, deeming it the safest, and nibbles on the edge of the crust.

Even as he resolves to try and be unaffected, Deimos rising to his feet has him tensing as he watches the beast leave the room. It truly seems like he doesn't mind Phainon being unattended.

He fills up on bread and water, even going as far as to take a few bites of cheese and cured meat before setting out. Since Deimos had given him blanket permission to explore the mansion, he's going to make the most of it.

The hallways are empty, devoid of any servants or human touch, and he finds himself wondering about Tribbie. Is the doll still somewhere out there, or had she been discovered by Deimos? Surely he wouldn't hurt her, seeing as she's a little trinket, right?

He shivers when a cool breeze blows past him. It's only now that he realises that the fool that he is, he'd forgotten to change into clothes that actually suited the weather. Even if it didn't snow, Aedes Elysiae is prone to winter rains and, during one memorable year, hailstones that had rattled musically across the shingles of their roofs.

Just recalling the memories brings a smile to his lips. He'd been young then, and still in awe of the world around him. The hailstones had almost been like magic, and he'd spent the afternoon collecting balls of ice like they were chicken eggs only to have them melt through his basket.

"Um…hello!"

The voice jolts him out of his thoughts. Floating in front of him is a little embroidered doll of a unicorn, its wings flapping hard to keep its…er, rather rotund body afloat.

"You're not allowed in there!" The unicorn flaps in a circle around his head. "So please, don't enter? Deimos won't like it!"

"Is this the western spire?"

"Yes. What's inside is very, very important to him, so outsiders aren't allowed in. I hope you can understand."

"I was just exploring, that's all. Please don't misunderstand, I wouldn't overstep my boundaries."

The unicorn sags in relief, its wings stalling for a moment before it continues flapping desperately again, trying to regain lost height.

"That's a good thing. My name is Hyacine. You must be the new guest that Tribbie spoke of?"

"You spoke to Tribbie? Is she safe?"

Hyacine giggles. "What a silly question. We're all safer in this house than anywhere else in this forest. Would you like a tour?"

A tour certainly beats wandering around aimlessly, and Hyacine had offered…

"Sure."

Hyacine does a little twirl before speeding off down the halls.

She takes him to the kitchens, pointing out where the pantry is so he can get himself a snack if he's hungry, though the invisible hands of the kitchen will always ensure that there is hot food on the table every meal.

The bedrooms and various guest rooms are closed, and Hyacine brushes over them with just one line explaining their purpose.

It's when they step into the study that things start to get weird.

"And this is Professor." Hyacine lands on the table, nudging a quill. "He's like us."

The quill is an exotic green feather that shimmers with a red undertone, capped with a gold nib. As Phainon stares, it shivers for a moment before it jumps out of the inkpot and begins to write. The handwriting is smooth, and Phainon squints to read the glittering green ink.

My name is Anaxagoras. You will address me as Professor Anaxagoras.

"Professor Anaxa is very intelligent," Hyacine whispers. "Even Deimos comes to ask him for help sometimes."

Deimos is someone willing to learn, so I am willing to teach. He is my best student.

"He is your only student, Professor," Hyacine replies. "But you have…oh, my apologies. I never asked your name, did I?"

"Phainon. It's good to meet the two of you."

"Phainon!" Hyacine twirls on the spot. "It's a lovely name."

Why are you here? I'm sure that you didn't come here for an all expenses paid vacation.

"Oh…I came here to free my father, actually. He disappeared last night, and the only hunter who returned kept talking about a beast."

He gives them a brief rundown of the situation, and Hyacine's wings droop.

"Please don't think badly of Deimos. He's been living alone for a long time, and the–"

Hyacine.

Anaxa's pen all but slashes the word into the air, and the stuffed toy quietens. Phainon looks between the two of them.

"What? What's wrong with Deimos?"

Anaxa drops back into the inkwell, going silent, and Hyacine looks at the pen before drifting forward.

"Perhaps we should leave Professor Anaxa to himself," she says gently. "Have you seen the library?"

When Hyacine mentioned the library, he had nebulous thoughts of an enormous volume of books, shelves higher than he can reach and a general feeling of austerity, much like an enormous schoolhouse might feel.

Deimos' library is nothing like that.

Sure, there are still shelves so tall that a complicated system of ladders and walkways have been installed, allowing for the higher shelves to be reached, and the sheer number of books in this place boggles his mind, but when he looks down, there are soft cushions scattered around, as well as blankets draped over low couches. Lamps hidden in small corners cast a soft, warm glow over the whole place, and it smells like paper and ink.

"Woah." Phainon turns in small steps, drinking in the sight before his eyes. "I've never seen so many books in one place before."

"You're welcome to read them."

The sudden voice from behind has him jumping almost a foot into the air, turning around to see Deimos looming behind him.

"Warn a guy before you sneak up on him, please!" Phainon rests a hand over his chest, trying to soothe his rabbiting heart rate.

Deimos blinks languidly. "Just like how you warned me before breaking into my house?"

"That!" Phainon bristles before deflating. "I'll admit, I shouldn't have done that, but I was desperate."

"You were not a threat, regardless."

Then, as though he hadn't just called Phainon weak, he turns and approaches the shelf, tilting his head sideways to read the spines of the books. He glances at Hyacine, who doesn't move, but seems to be giving him a shrug.

"Hyacine,I didn't know you acted as a tour guide," Deimos says without looking back, and the stuffed toy chirps.

"You weren't making it easy for Phainon to entertain himself, Deimos." Hyacine drifts closer. "You've also been lonely, haven't you?"

"I have you, and Tribios, and Professor Anaxagoras," Deimos grumbles. "I don't need anyone else."

"You know that's not what I meant."

Phainon watches Deimos interact with the plushie while browsing through the shelves, occasionally picking out a book here and there. When he has a stack of books, Deimos makes his way to a shallow indent in the ground, where a large rug is spread across the stone floor and decorated with a dozen throw pillows.

"Are you going to just stand there like an ornament?"

He approaches Deimos and carelessly plucks a book from his pile, ignoring the growl that rattles the windowpanes.

"'Castrum Kremnos: Military Conquests and Strategies'," Phainon reads out loud, then huffs. "I didn't know you could read."

For a moment, stunned silence rings out in the wake of his comment. Hyacine is so shocked that she forgets to flap, falling to the carpeted area with a squeak. Deimos' face doesn't lend itself to expressions very well, but his eyes are wide.

"Not for the first time, I wonder if there's something wrong with your brain," Deimos says slowly, shaking his head. "Is there?"

"I have fallen a few times, but I'm guessing that's not what you want to hear?" Phainon grins and returns the book to the pile. "No, sorry. My brain is perfectly fine."

"Could've fooled me," Deimos snorts.

Phainon begins picking through the books on the lower shelves, and quickly, he figures out the system. Sections are dedicated to genres, and within the sections, they're further divided based on author and subject matter.

It is, all in all, a very comprehensive library, lovingly curated and cared for.

He eventually finds an illustrated book of fairytales, and carries it over to where Deimos is curled up.

"Where's Hyacine?" He asks, settling down on a cushion and opening the book.

"She left. The other inhabitants tend to do whatever they want."

"Oh."

They fall into silence, Phainon's attention wholly taken by the book in his hands. He doesn't understand the language that the book's written in, but the pictures are vivid, easily painting a tale that he can understand.

Nikador pursues a human princess, only for her to leap off the cliff when she beheld their monstrous visage, believing her husband to be dead. Heartbroken and grieving, her brothers had attempted to hunt the Titan down, causing their entire city-state to be eliminated.

The tale of a lion and oryx, locked forever in eternal pursuit until they died, and even then their spirits continue to chase each other down, thus giving birth to the cycles of night and day.

"These are some morbid fairytales," he comments when he reaches the end. "Is this even suitable for children to read?"

"That book is written in Kremnoan. Do you even understand what it's saying?"

"Not a lick, but the pictures are there for a reason." He flips open to the first page. "You know Kremnoan, don't you? Why don't you teach me?"

"Teach you," Deimos says. "Me."

"Yes. You said you knew how to read, so presumably, you're fluent in Kremnoan, seeing as you're reading…" Phainon cranes his neck. "An atlas, apparently."

"You do not read an atlas. You observe." Deimos tilts the thick book towards Phainon. In his hands, a book that he'd have to rest on his knees to read looks no larger than a stone slate. "You learn from an atlas."

"There are no words in an atlas, Deimos." Phainon leans back. "Come on. I promise I'm a fast learner. I'll pick up the syntax in no time!"

"I refuse."

"What? Afraid your oh-so-perfect reputation as a teacher will be tarnished?"

Deimos growls. His entire body shifts, and Phainon yelps as the warm surface he'd been reclining on ripples. Deimos' back, he realises. He'd been pressed up against the beast's flank, and he hadn't even realised.

Now, Phainon isn't a small guy. His growth spurt had seen him shooting up in height until even Audata's darning skills couldn't keep him in clothes that fit, for a period of time. He towers over most of the adults in the village, and he's quite proud of that.

But right now, lying on his back and pinned down by a hand on his torso, he's never felt smaller.

Deimos is huge. Almost unfairly so, and he knows it, if the way he watches Phainon struggle is any indication. A predator toying with its prey, knowing that the outcome had already been set in stone.

"Prepare yourself, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae," Deimos rumbles, and he feels a jolt deep in his stomach.

"Uh huh? Prepare myself for what?" He asks breathlessly. His smile is possibly unhinged. "Are you going to eat me?"

"No. You wouldn't taste good anyway."

"I would probably taste delicious, I'll have you know!"

Deimos chuffs and sits back on his haunches.

"You should pick up the basics first before asking me to teach you. As you are now, you are not worthy to be taught by me."

The next day, he seeks out Hyacine, Tribbie and Anaxa for their help. They throw themselves into the task with great enthusiasm, Anaxa in particular seems to be the one most pleased by this, although Phainon can't tell if it's because he's expressed an eagerness to learn or because of some other reason.

Language is not my field of study, but lesson plans are always easy enough to write. How far have you progressed?

Anaxa supervises his writing skills, once he's mastered the basics of the alphabet. He learns that there are different versions of the language from when the Kremnoan empire expanded and its language married itself to a dozen different dialects spoken by the people within their empire's lands, giving birth to regional differences. He learns that the original Kremnoan language had been mostly lost due to an enormous fire burning down most of its grand library, and that even now, historians are struggling to decipher most of the ancient texts.

He wonders if Deimos had known someone from Castrum Kremnos. Surely someone close to him had been from there, otherwise, why would he have so many books in that language? A sour feeling prickles his heart whenever he thinks of that, and he resolves to push that thought away whenever it comes around.

Tribbie is perhaps the most excited one about his education. With her, he gets his real world practice in, seeing as she's finally found a partner to narrate her stories and play with her.

"De always offers to tell us stories, but we feel bad," Tribbie tells him one day, when they're taking a break from reenacting a storybook that Tribbie had picked.

"So when you heard I was practicing Kremnoan, you rushed over to have a different person tell you stories?" Phainon clicks his tongue in faux disappointment. "Naughty."

"Snowy!" The dolls tumble around, and he catches one of them to make sure that they wouldn't fall off the pillow. "That's not what we mean! And we're older than you, of course we have to supervise your studies!"

Well, if that's what the dolls want to believe, he'll play along with their little fantasy.

Hyacine too, plays her part by keeping him fed and rested, and reminding him to take breaks from reading. He's spending more and more time in the library now, especially since he's starting to get a grasp on the Kremnoan language. Despite being more straightforward and thus easier to learn, some words and phrases are layered with meaning and dependent on being well-versed in Kremnos' culture to understand the context in which it is used. Anaxa had tilted from side to side when he brought this up, which is about as close as he gets to scoffing.

The Kremnoan language, while brusque, does not mean that it is completely devoid of any metaphor or flowery prose. It's mostly an exaggeration by Okhema's Council of Elders.

"Are they hated?" He asks idly, twirling a quill—not Anaxa, he'd made that mistake once and gotten stabbed for his troubles—between his fingers.

Feared is more accurate. Castrum Kremnos is a formidable opponent, and yet, Okhema has chosen to make an enemy out of them. Right now, Amphoreus is in a state of political unrest.

Political unrest or not, it doesn't extend to Deimos' mansion, which is insulated from the outside world, partly due to its remote location, partly due to the legends of the beast keeping others away.

Well…sometimes.

In one of the rare moments where Deimos had passed by him in the hallways, Phainon had taken the chance to ask about the outside world.

"More bounty hunters have come as of late," Deimos tells him. "They're setting up traps in the forest."

They both know what the bounty hunters are here for, and thus, Phainon doesn't bring it up.

Still, it doesn't take long for the trouble to reach their doorstep.

It's been about two weeks since Phainon's first day here when he gets it into his mind that he wants to do some gardening. The brambly, overgrown mess had already been irking him when he snuck into the mansion, and he feels more comfortable now.

So the morning of this fateful day sees him marching out with a borrowed pair of boots, Tribbie hitching a ride on a harness that's wrapped around Hyacine. He'd fashioned it when Tribbie mentioned how difficult moving around the mansion was, and Hyacine had seemed eager enough to try it out.

"Snowy, what are you going to do?" Tribbie asks, peering over his shoulder as he sets down the gardening shears that he'd found.

"The grass has gotten really long, so I'm going to trim it down."

"By yourself?" Hyacine murmurs. Phainon grins at the toys.

"I used to work on a farm and help out my parents. Compared to that, this is nothing."

If anything, it'll be almost nostalgic.

Phainon gets to work, set on clearing out at least the grass around the main path leading up to the mansion. Hyacine and Tribbie help him from the sky, spotting anything that rustles in the grass and reporting it to him. Mostly grass snakes, though there's an occasional squirrel that Tribbie squeals over.

The manual labour sinks into his bones, and he hisses under his breath as his muscles ache. He'd definitely gotten out of shape after two weeks of practically no heavy activity, but he can't say he didn't enjoy it either.

Unbidden, his thoughts drift to Deimos. They tended to do that a lot recently, and he'd long since resigned himself to never meeting Deimos again. Even though they live in the same house, the difference between them is far too large, both literally and metaphorically. If Deimos wanted to, he'd be able to hide away until Phainon dies of old age.

That thought gives him pause.

Why had he assumed that he would grow old and die in this house? Deimos had said that he was free to go whenever he wanted, hadn't he? At first, Phainon hadn't taken that offer seriously because that definitely sounded like a trap, but now…

His hands still.

He could leave.

Just put down the shears and walk out of the gate, and keep walking until he sees the smokestacks in Aedes Elysiae. The forest is easy enough to navigate; he's not ashamed to say that he'd spent more than a few nights fantasising about how he would go home, right down to the details. He could go back to Cyrene, his mother and father, Piso and Livia and everyone that he'd grown up with.

But then he thinks of Tribbie and Hyacine. They would be sad that he left. Anaxa would be so angry with him for not completing his lesson plan, and Deimos…

Deimos would be alone again. No one to talk to, no one to fill the halls of his mansion with footsteps and chatter.

He lifts his foot. It hovers there, waiting for him to make his choice. But in the end, fate makes the choice for him.

"Snowy! People!" Tribbie hisses. She's so panicked that she almost topples out of the harness, and it's only Hyacine's skills that prevent that from happening. Phainon moves quickly. He shoves all of his gardening materials into the long grass and dives in to hide from them, reaching up to hold Hyacine and Tribbie close to his chest. One– no, two people approach him, their conversation becoming clearer.

"…sure about this?"

"Stop questioning me. I told you, didn't I? Those villagers were almost frothing at the mouth. Shouting about how some beast spirited away one of them."

"And you believed it?"

"'course not. That villager of theirs probably fell down a valley and snapped their neck or something. They're probably nothing but bones now. Still, if we come here and bring something back for them, they might give us lodging and food for the night."

"Harsh."

The footsteps stop right outside where he's hiding, and he holds his breath.

"But you see, as a hunter, you hear stories. And the legends surrounding this forest…well, they're quite interesting. All of them swear that they've heard horrific howls, echoing around the trees."

"What? So the beast…"

"Probably not as large as they make it out to be, but hey. It's probably an overgrown bear or something. If we take it down, it'll tide us through winter and then some, I reckon."

A pause. Then:

"Hey, does the grass look cut to you?"

Phainon curses up a storm inside his head.

"Huh." A sniff. "Smells like it too. You think someone lives here?"

"Maybe the beast does its own gardening?"

"Nah. Maybe it's some sorcerer's pet that got off its leash."

Phainon grits his teeth. They're talking about Deimos like he's some kind of wild animal, and it ignites something ugly within him that claws at his ribs.

"Whatever. Let's go scout out the mansion. If there's an owner, we say hello, explain the situation, and get the hell out of here."

"And if there isn't one?"

There's a click that Phainon recognises: flint striking steel, and he almost gasps. These bounty hunters had brought firearms. Those things are expensive and gunpowder even more so, which means that they're probably well-off.

And a rich bounty hunter means that they're good at their job.

"Well, now. No one would miss a rabid beast in this forest, would they?"

Phainon remains stock still in the grass until he's certain he can no longer hear them. Only then does he exhale slowly, his breath whistling out between his teeth, and release Hyacine and Tribbie from his grasp. The former shakes out her wings before lifting into the air, but Tribbie remains in his hand, the painted wood of the doll cool to the touch.

"We have to warn De," Tribbie whispers. "They want to do bad things to him."

"I think he already knows," Hyacine says. "He's been scouting around recently."

"Right." He looks at the two of them. "But we should still tell him anyway."

They hurry back to the house; Phainon briefly contemplates taking the gardening shears with him, but ultimately, he decides not to in the end.

The main door had long been fused shut by a combination of time and the weather, which meant they needed to take the longer way and go through a side door normally reserved for servants. The detour means that when Phainon emerges into the main hall, Hyacine and Tribbie by his side, it's from a side hallway under the sweeping staircase, granting him a full view of what's happening before him.

A broken window clearly shows their entrance into the house, and their guns are pointed at Deimos, whose fur is standing on end. Phainon's confused for a moment as to why Deimos wouldn't just run away before Hyacine makes a sound of distress.

"His leg–!"

Phainon looks closer, and his stomach sinks. Deimos' hind leg is caught in a trap, the teeth of the trap digging into fur and presumably, flesh. The first hunter that he barrels into goes down with a shout, but he slams his fist into the man's face, punching him hard enough that he can feel cartilage snapping under his knuckles. The other man rushes at him, but he gets off the hunter under him and tackles the man's legs, sending the two of them sprawling onto the ground.

"What the hell!?" The man that he's grappling with yells. "There's a guy here!"

His partner doesn't answer, and if the nasal sobs are anything to go by, he's not going to be answering any time soon.

"Deimos," he gasps, turning to the beast. "Your leg."

A punch lands squarely on his cheek, and he snarls and turns back to the fight. Still, Deimos' voice floats over to him, as clear as if he's speaking right beside Phainon's ear.

"Deal with them first."

He doesn't have to be told twice. Phainon rears back and headbutts the hunter under him so hard that the sound echoes crisply through the main hall. The man slumps in his grip, blood dripping from a patch on his head and his eyes rolled up so far back that Phainon can barely see his pupils.

He turns to the other hunter with the broken nose, who's staring at them with wide, terrified eyes, blood running down his chin and his nose so swollen that his breathing comes out in a high-pitched whistle.

"Take your friend and leave. I don't want to see you back here," Phainon says, and the man nods frantically.

As the two of them stumble out of the door, Phainon catches a glimpse of green. Tribbie must've gone to get Anaxa; that's good. They would ensure that the hunters actually leave instead of staking the mansion out. And in the meantime…

"Deimos."

He rushes over to the trap. It's the kind used for disabling large game and predators, and he finds the release switch easily enough, snapping the trap open so that Deimos can gingerly withdraw his leg.

"Don't lick!" Phainon shoves Deimos' snout away from his wound. "This trap's dirty. Who knows what the hunters have done with it."

"I'll be fine."

"Hyacine?" He calls out, ignoring the other's grumbles. "Do we have a first aid kit in the mansion?"

"We do!" She zips off immediately, only to return moments later with a box balanced on her back.

"Thank you. Is there a place where I can get hot water and clean cloth?"

"You two are wasting–"

"The kitchen. I can take you two there."

Deimos grumbles, but when Phainon tugs at him, he goes, very conspicuously keeping weight off his injured limb.

The kitchen that Hyacine guides them to definitely had the things he needed, and he busies himself with drawing a tub of boiling hot water first. The wound is irregular, but it'd been mostly shallow, with only a few parts where it'd actually cut into flesh.

"I thought you would leave," Deimos says.

"Leave?"

"For your village. I assumed that you would take the chance to escape from my mansion. Those bounty hunters were no ordinary people; I'm sure that they would've be able to kill me."

"Well…I would be lying if I said I didn't consider it, these past few days. Even got as far as the gate, actually, when I met the hunters." He wills his hands to be steady as he rinses the wounds out, grimacing when the water turns pink. "They said some pretty awful things about you."

"And that was what made you want to stay?"

"No. I wanted to stay because I realised that it isn't true, Deimos." He dabs at the wound, wiping away the excess blood that had welled up. "They said you were no better than a wild animal, good for nothing but to be hunted and mounted as a trophy. But if they'd just meet you, they would see—"

"—a beast." Deimos chuffs. "You are perhaps the only one naive enough to see my face and think me capable of being bargained with."

"And look where that got me." He snips the bandage and leans back to admire his handiwork. "Does it hurt?"

"Pain is temporary to this body of mine."

"That's not what I asked."

"It doesn't matter."

"Of course it does." Phainon begins to pack the first aid kit up, soaking the needle and thread in purified ambrosia to disinfect it. "If you're hurting, then tell me, and I'll figure out a way to fix you up. You gain nothing from keeping this to yourself."

"And your hand?"

"Uh?" Phainon looks down at his hands. His knuckles are split, and now that Deimos had mentioned it, his forehead is throbbing with a dull ache. Maybe he shouldn't have headbutted the man, but it was the fastest way to knock him out.

"It'll be fine," he says. "I'll put some ointment over my hands later, but your leg needed attention more urgently."

Deimos remains silent, even as he finishes packing the kit up and turns to head out. But when Phainon's hand lands on the knob, he speaks.

"Come with me."

There is no explanation, nothing that would give him a hint to what Deimos wanted to do. And yet, he goes anyway, trailing beside Deimos and keeping a critical eye on his foot as he limps along.

It takes him a few moments to realise, but when he realises where they're headed towards, he shoots Deimos a disbelieving look.

The door to the western tower looks the same as it had when he'd accidentally stumbled upon it, but this time, Deimos opens the door easily.

"For a tower that's off limits, the locks sure don't seem to work very well."

"Did you think that this tower is protected only by physical means?" Deimos steps through the door, which seems to warp ever so slightly so that he could fit through. Phainon doesn't quite understand what he's talking about until he passes through the door. A shiver rolls across his skin, raising the hairs on his arm, and he shudders.

"The stairs are steep," Deimos warns. "Watch yourself."

They begin climbing. Deimos hadn't brought a light, but the air within the tower seems lighter, somehow, and it's bright enough that Phainon can still see ahead of him, watching Deimos pad up the steps smoothly.

Higher and higher they go, until the air begins to brighten and Phainon can begin to make out more delicate shapes.

When they reach the top of the tower and Deimos moves aside, Phainon's breath is stolen from his lungs.

Before him, a lily glows in the darkness, its petals shimmering with a faint, golden hue. A bell jar is placed over it, and Deimos circles around so that he can stand over it, a paw coming up to brush against the glass.

"What…is this?" Phainon breathes. The scene before him is hauntingly beautiful, like a story right out of the fairytales that he'd read for Tribbie.

"My weak spot," Deimos says. "Once all the petals from the lily fall, my time will be up."

As he watches, one pale petal detaches from the head, drifting down and landing at the bottom of the bell jar.

"Nine left," Phainon murmurs. "What happens when the last petal falls?"

"Who knows? I only know that I should protect this flower with my life." A paw comes around the bell jar, curling around it protectively. "I'm not sure what'll happen if someone kills it before it sheds all its petals, but it can be nothing good."

"Oh."

Words and lines flit through his brain, each one being discarded for a variety of reasons.

Deimos had shared something very important with him, and Phainon can keenly feel the weight of his trust bearing down on his shoulders. But he will carry it, if only so he won't disappoint Deimos. Time spent with this strange creature means that he'd had time to form his own thoughts on him, and he finds that Deimos is a being of contradictions.

He loves sweet things, but still consumes large amounts of meat like a predator would.

His form might be large, but he's exceedingly gentle, so gentle that Phainon wonders how much time he'd had to practice restraining his strength.

And…despite what he says about his hideous visage, Phainon thinks that there's a certain regality to him. Perhaps only Deimos could pull it off, with how he seems to exude the air of nobility.

But Deimos doesn't seem to want an answer from him, and Phainon doesn't know what to say, so he swallows the heavy words until they sit in his belly and instead says:

"Do you want me to read to you? I've been practicing Kremnoan. I promise I won't let you down."

Deimos stares at him. The only thing that Phainon can see are his golden eyes, glowing in the darkness, and he swallows tightly.

"Very well," Deimos says. "Let's see if you're worthy of my respect."

"I swear I'll prove myself."

"Less talking, more action."

Phainon stifles a laugh as he follows Deimos out of the west tower and towards the library.

"I thought you wanted me to practice speaking Kremnoan to you? In case you've forgotten, we need to speak to convey meaning."

"That tongue of yours is as long as a serpent's. Take care that you do not trip on it."

Nothing really changes after that, only…

It seems as though Deimos is now seeking his company.

They read in the library, with Phainon acting out the stories and Deimos correcting his pronunciation at times, though he's pleased to say that those times are getting fewer each chance he gets.

"You should come visit my library, when you get the chance."

"You have another library?" He looks up from where he'd been practicing with a list of feats that former warriors of Castrum Kremnos had performed. It's a very long list.

"Yes. Although…" Deimos growls in frustration. "I've forgotten where it is exactly."

"No worries. It's not like I can finish reading through this library, even with my entire life ahead of me."

Whenever Phainon gets restless, he'd head out to the front gardens and tear through the grass while Deimos lounged in the alcove just before the front doors open into the main hall—as it turns out, those imposing doors had been sealed with the same magic as the door to the western tower.

When he asks Deimos why he would do that, the beast pauses licking his fur to stare blankly at Phainon as though he'd suddenly said he wanted to eat the grass he was cutting.

"Why would I leave my door unlocked all the time?"

"…Fair enough."

The days pass easily enough, and Phainon almost forgets about the lily. At least, until he gets to his bedroom one night to face down Anaxa, Hyacine and Tribbie.

"Um…" He looks between the three items. "What's wrong?"

"Snowy!" Tribbie wails, rocking from side to side. "You're running out of time!"

"What?"

"Deimos' flower is on its last four petals," Hyacine says. "We were hoping that you could break the curse on him."

"A curse?" Phainon echoes. "Wait, what? Deimos is cursed? And why me? Surely there are people more suited to the job?"

Goodness, your self-esteem needs some work. The curse is designed to ensure that he will lose himself over time. A particularly tricky bit of magic, able to be cast over long distances…for a price.

The pen shivers, its feathers fluffing up before they settle back into calmness again.

As the petals fall, the power that gives us awareness will fade alongside it. We can only stay like this for another three days, at most. Afterwards, you're on your own.

"What!? I can't break a curse in three days! That's impossible!" Phainon blusters. "And you'll die if I can't break it?"

"No!" Hyacine hurries to assure him. "We won't die, we'll just…be unable to communicate with you, that's all."

"But if you don't, De…" Tribbie's voice wobbles. "He'll…"

Hush.

The pen slashes through the air, and the tip of the quill jabs towards him.

We are only asking. You do not have an obligation to save him, Phainon. Nevertheless, it would be nice to be able to speak without writing everything out.

"Wait, what's going to happen if I don't break the curse?"

"He'll lose his mind," Hyacine says quietly. "And then perhaps he'll be killed one day, when he rages across the land."

Phainon gapes.

He'd thought the worst case scenario was that Deimos would die, or something along those lines, but for him to lose himself and truly become a beast…

That is possibly a fate worse than death.

"Is…do you have any hints about the spell?" He asks weakly, and Anaxa quivers.

No. He has been adamant about keeping the curse to himself. But if it's you, Phainon, he will give in. I'm sure of it.

"Where is he now?"

"He left."

Those two words send a cold rush down his spine.

"Left?" Phainon repeats hysterically. "He doesn't leave the mansion."

Even when Phainon had repeatedly invited the other to join him in gardening, Deimos had been content just lounging on the patio, watching him toil away.

He only leaves at night, and after he makes sure that you're asleep.

"He…" A laugh bubbles up in his chest, and he tamps it down. "When did he leave? Where is he headed?"

"We're not sure," Tribbie says sadly. "All of us are bound to this place, so we can't go outside with him."

"But he shouldn't have gone far!" Hyacine chimes in. "He just left!"

"It's fine." Phainon straightens his back. "Thank you, all of you, but I'll take it from here now. I'll find him and break his curse, no matter what it takes."

Deimos deserves that much, at the very least. To live well as himself, surrounded by his friends.

"Wait!" Tribbie jumps up and down on his bed. "It's night right now. You won't be able to see anything!"

"But I can't– every second I spend here is another second that Deimos could be–" A lump in his throat suffocates the rest of his sentence, and Hyacine drifts closer.

"We know," she says. "We meant to say that with the remnants of our power, we can bless you to make things a little easier."

"We are priests from Janusopolis, you know!" Tribbie begins to glow, gold outlining the edge of the wooden doll. "With our blessings, your heart will lead you true!"

"With the blessings of the Sky, the very air around you shall aid you," Hyacine says, the plush toy flashing pink.

This is not a blessing, but more of a reminder. I grant you clarity, Phainon. Remember who you are, and speak truthfully. Now, hurry.

Phainon nods. There's no time to thank them, so he bolts out of his room and down the corridors. Pulling on his shoes wastes precious seconds, but the moment he steps out of the gate, a shimmering rainbow line extends before him, reaching through the trees. Hyacine's blessing, no doubt.

He runs now, not to escape from the mansion, but to save the beast within. The veil of Evernight makes it far more difficult for him to track Deimos down through prints alone, but Tribbie's blessing hums within his chest.

He picks a direction, prays to Janus, and begins to run. Soon enough, hints begin to make themselves clear: enraged roars, yelling, and a distant glow in the forest, flickering like fire.

Phainon leaps over a log and comes face to face with a scene of chaos. Dark, shadowy waves of soldiers are surging up to meet Deimos, who bats them away like they're a swarm of gnats. Weapons shatter, spears are snapped in half, and the soldiers that fall to the ground struggle to their feet before rushing Deimos again.

He's trying not to hurt them, Phainon realises. His attacks are far weaker than what he'd unleashed against the bandits, and he's only backing away, not charging forward.

But eventually, fatigue catches up to him. His swings are slower, and frothy drool drips from between his jaws as he growls in warning. More and more weapons are making it through his defences, and when a blade sinks into his ribs, Phainon sees red.

The situation is chaotic enough that he can slip through their ranks, pick up a sword from the ground and shoulder-check a soldier out of the way to stand in front of Deimos before anyone realises what happened.

"Don't come any closer." Despite the cold night pressing in before him, Phainon's hand is steady. The rage that burns within his chest warms him despite the chill that permeates the air, and he chances a look behind.

There's blood. So much blood stains the ground, and Deimos is curled up and unmoving. Spitfire rage hisses and sparks within his chest, demanding an outlet. It roars for an equal amount of blood to be spilled as compensation.

A soldier comes forward, and when he speaks, Phainon recognises it as Kremnoan.

"Please, sir, whatever magic that thing's put you under, we can undo it." The soldier takes another step, and it's only because his hands are empty that Phainon doesn't attack. "We have a powerful witch who is working with us. They can help you, so you don't have to be afraid."

"I'm not under a spell, but I wonder if your sight has been blighted." Phainon replies in Kremnoan. "Open your eyes! See for yourself that this is not a monster to be hunted like some kind of prey!"

"Sir–" The soldier's interrupted when someone emerged from the ranks, marching towards him with purpose. Immediately, the other soldier retreats, allowing Phainon to observe the man who's striding towards him.

His hair is grey, with a few streaks of white, and he bears the countenance of a man who'd been unfairly aged by stress and time. Still, his eyes are steely, and when he stares Phainon down, he knows the other man is observing him as well.

"I am Krateros, commander of this detachment from Kremnos. Might I know who you are?"

"Phainon of Aedes Elysiae."

"Phainon." Krateros' lips tighten. "Do you know just what kind of evil you are protecting?"

"Evil? No. Pray tell, enlighten me."

"That thing kidnapped our Crown Prince Mydeimos." Krateros doesn't snarl, but it's a close thing. "It took him from his chambers, and left nothing but claw marks as it escaped undetected from Castrum Kremnos."

He blinks slowly, digesting the information, but Krateros isn't done yet.

"To save our prince, we must slay the beast."

The army marches forward one step, but they stop when a growl deep enough to shake the earth emanates from behind him. He pays it no heed.

"Your prince's name…is Mydeimos?" Phainon repeats, puzzled. "But…"

The pieces of the puzzle are slotting together, and he's almost solved it. He just needs–

"I am the prince that they speak of." Deimos—no, Mydeimos'—snout comes to rest heavy against his shoulder. "But they are cursed to see me as nothing but vermin, just as I am cursed to wear the form of a beast. A witch from Okhema has chosen to wage war against Castrum Kremnos, and this is her chosen method: to wield my people like a blade against me."

"How do you break it?" Phainon whispers. "Surely a curse like this should have an impossible condition to fulfill, right?"

"Only true love will break this spell cast over me. But it must be given freely to this visage, and before the lily in the west wing withers entirely."

"How many petals remain?" Phainon asks, and Mydei growls.

"Don't."

"Mydei."

"Don't. I do not beg, Phainon. But please…don't."

Phainon takes a deep breath. Holds it while he faces Krateros and the rest of the Kremnoan detachment, then turns to face Mydei. He exhales.

Just like breathing. As easy as that.

"I love you, Mydei. I think I've loved you since you laughed at the stupid voices I do for stories, and I'll love you even if you become a monster."

There is no true word for love in Kremnoan, at least not within his shallow knowledge of the language, but there are a thousand ways to express affection in Aedes Elysian. For that word, he speaks his own tongue, hoping that Mydei will understand his intentions.

"Phainon, you–" He cuts off abruptly when his head snaps backwards, and an inhuman howl rips free from his throat. A series of sickening crackles come from his limbs, contorted into painful angles, and Phainon hurries to his side, clutching at whatever part he can reach and murmuring mindless words of comfort to Mydei.

Mydei doesn't even seem to be cognizant, his pants heavy and ragged as he claws at the ground, carving grooves into the soft mud. Something is roiling under his skin, and Phainon buries his face into his thick mane, wishing that he could shoulder some of the pain for him.

It hurts that he has to watch Mydei suffer like this, that transforming back into a man pains him so terribly. The fur falls away from his body, revealing tanned skin lined with dark red tattoos, and his body shrinks down to a more humanoid size. His hair is the same colour as his mane, and his eyes too, remain golden, even though they're currently foggy and unfocused. Phainon tugs his cloak tighter around him and adjusts himself, trying to shield Mydei with his frame.

"Oh, Titans," he breathes, cupping the man's cheek in his hand. "How do you feel, Mydei?"

Mydei doesn't answer, and fear rears its ugly head again. Maybe the spell had gone wrong. Maybe something else had gone wrong, and Mydei isn't cured. Maybe Phainon's love hadn't been enough, maybe he's not the one–

"Stop overthinking. I can hear your thoughts running in circles," Mydei rasps, and a gasp ripples through the Kremnoan detachment. A hysterical laugh bubbles up in his throat, but Phainon suppresses it.

"My prince." Krateros' voice trembles. "You…You…"

"Patience, Krateros. There are matters that require my concern."

Phainon clicks his tongue in annoyance. Mydei's still half-sprawled over him, his body shaking with minute trembles, and he's already trying to give out orders? That wouldn't do.

He makes sure that the cloak is carefully arranged before he sweeps Mydei up into a bridal carry, ignoring his startled shout and grinning back at the gobsmacked army.

"Mydei must be tired after that transformation. How about you all come in and make yourself comfortable, and he can get down to business after some rest and clothes?"

Without waiting for their answer, he takes Mydei back into the mansion. For the entire duration of the short walk, Mydei's eyes don't leave his face at all, not even when he sets the man down on the bed of a guest bedroom and checks the wardrobe for any spare robes that he can use.

For a Crown Prince returning to his people, he'd need to look the part, so Phainon had picked out a few pieces that matched the Kremnoan colours.

When he carries it over to Mydei, the other man snorts.

"So you do know how to pick out clothes, after all."

"Hey, I'm not colourblind," he protests, laying out the fabrics on the bed and turning away so that Mydei can dress. "I just care more for the meaning of the clothes than the colours."

"A bold way of saying that you dress like a bird trying to impress its mate." A few moments of rustling. "Purple and yellow while gardening? You should be thankful that the courtyard is deserted."

"Oh? Are you saying that I managed to capture your heart, then?"

Mydei huffs, and they subside into an awkward silence. Phainon fidgets, unsure if he should leave or wait until the other man has finished dressing. Before he can decide, he hears a hum from Mydei.

"Hm. Perhaps there is hope for you after all."

He turns around, and his breath escapes him.

Mydei is beautiful.

Perhaps no sane person would describe him as such, considering his build is more akin to a warrior than a delicate maiden, but to him, Mydei perfectly encapsulates that word. His hair is reminiscent of his mane, and his eyes are still golden, perhaps as a side effect of his transformation.

The red tunic highlights his skin, warm and bronzed by the sun, and Phainon blinks dazedly.

"…You really look like a prince."

Mydei frowns.

"Did you hit your head on the way to me?" He says, scandalised. "I am a prince."

"No, but you look–" Here, he makes a gesture. "Sorry. I'm really not used to seeing you as a human."

"That's no surprise," Mydei snorts. "I never even told you that I was once a human."

"Why didn't you?"

Mydei looks taken aback by the question, and then troubled.

"I…suppose I forgot," he says. "Towards the end, things begin to slip my mind. My mother's face. The voices of my friends. The line between human and beast began to blur for me."

"Mydei…"

"But," he says, meeting Phainon's eyes, "I remembered you. Even when you stood in front of me, I remembered not to attack you."

They're interrupted by a knock at the door, and Phainon wonders how they managed to find him before looking down at his boots. Right. He'd probably tracked mud across the entire length of the mansion.

"My prince," the voice says. "We await you in the main hall."

Mydei looks at Phainon. He opens his mouth, as though to say something, and then—

"And then?" Livia asks, her eyes wide. "And then what happened?"

Phainon laughs helplessly. "Livia, you know what happens. You made me tell you this story at least a thousand times."

"Because it's so wonderful!" The girl kicks her feet. "You should've gotten a happy ending!"

"I did." He yanks out a weed and tosses it to the side. "I got to come back to you all, and I'm healthy and whole."

"Yeah, but…" Livia pouts. "Your prince should've ridden back for you! They always do that in the stories. A white horse, shining armour, a large sword…"

The girl sighs again, and Phainon laughs and shakes his head.

He'd long given up on Mydei coming to find him.

That night, Mydei had told him everything: how he was trying to work with Aglaea of Okhema, alongside other allies, in order to broker a peace treaty. However, the Council of Elders opposed this so vehemently that they cursed him, forcing him to run from his people.

Anaxa, Tribbie and Hyacine had tried to help him, but as the curse progressed, he gradually lost interest in breaking it. After all, the professor had confirmed that upon death, his people would be released, so if he managed to find a way to kill himself, things could still progress as planned.

"We have to strike now," Mydei says. "Phainon, I know this is unfair of you, but–"

"No, I get it," he'd said, his voice light with forced brevity. "You have your duties. I won't keep you from them."

Mydei had hesitated then, before taking something out from his pocket and pressing it into his hands.

"This ring is a promise. I will return for you."

In the first year, he'd begged every wandering merchant, every circus troupe and every bard for news. From their words, he pieced together the situation. Hope had burned bright within his chest, all but consuming him in its passion.

In the second year, he'd waited. Breathlessly, endlessly, ardently. He'd wake up, his face already turned towards Castrum Kremnos' direction like a sunflower. He tells Cyrene the full story this year, sometime in the Month of Mourning. He cries into her shoulder in the Sacrament Courtyard until he feels like a wringed out rag. The flames had all but died down to embers.

In the third year, his passion mellowed out. It still burned, make no mistake, but now, Mydei fades into memory, into gentle, warm nostalgia. He appears in dreams in various forms: as the beast, as a human, and one time, as a chimeric combination of the two. Phainon no longer waits. He moves on. He learns to live.

And now, in the fourth year, he still loves Mydei. It has become a habit, as regular as the ring he wears under his shirt. It breathes with him, synced to the beating of his heart, and lives on as a gentle flame.

"PHAINON!!"

He's interrupted from his musings by Cyrene's screech. Livia yelps, almost falling off the fence and ruining her new dress, and Phainon shoves her so that she falls to the dusty road instead.

"Cyrene?"

She skids to a stop before him, her eyes shining.

"Soldiers," she breathes, her chest heaving with exertion. "Kremnoan."

That's all she needs to say.

He jumps to his feet, abandoning the plot that he'd been weeding, and runs.

There is no word in the Kremnoan language for 'love'. Their people are warriors, the softness of their language long sanded off to ensure that their words cut as deeply as their weapons. He understands this much from his short lessons with Anaxa and Mydei.

And yet, as he watches Mydei dismount from atop the dromas and approach him, a thousand words for love bubbles up within him. His tongue is heavy with the weight of the love in Aedes Elysian, Kremnoan, and common, and he brings a hand up to the helmet that hides Mydei's face from view. Dirt is still crusted on his hands, but Mydei's head tips down, allowing him to slide the helm off his head, revealing his hair and face.

"You're back," he says, his eyes twinkling. "I was beginning to think you'd forgotten me."

"Forget you? As if that's even possible," Mydei scoffs.

Phainon just laughs. His chest is so light it feels like he could fly. When he turns back to the rest of the villagers, they're all staring at him with various expressions of shock and amazement.

What a sight he must make: dirty, sweaty and grinning like a madman, standing next to the shining prince of Castrum Kremnos and a glittering square of soldiers accompanying him.

"Come meet my family? They've only ever heard of you, so I'm sure that they'll be glad to meet you."

The village is thrown into a frenzy.

A prince! Royalty, come to visit their humble abode!

Hastily, they rush to prepare a feast, and Phainon's heart warms when he sees Kremnoan soldiers coming up to help. It makes for a novel sight, seeing farmers alongside soldiers chopping vegetables, kneading dough and stirring pots.

He tries to help, but is shooed away by his mother, who takes one look at him and fixes him with a look so withering he shrinks back.

"Khaslana of Aedes Elysiae, you will clean yourself now or so help me, the Titans themselves won't save you!" She jabs a soup spoon at him for good measure, and Hieronymus stifles a laugh beside her.

"Yes, mama, papa," he mutters, properly chastened, and turns to Mydei. "Mydei, you–"

"I will be helping. It is hardly proper to leave the work to everyone else." Saying this, he's already removing his gauntlets, heedless of the protests that Audata and Hieronymus are saying, and marching towards the stoves with single-minded determination.

The feast is delicious, as expected. Phainon eats and drinks until he's pleasantly full, meandering between groups of people. They'd dragged tables and chairs out to one of the fields that lay fallow, and the food was served from the clearing in front of the Oronyx Titan's statue.

At some point, a soldier comes up to him, carrying a plate of kebabs.

"I owe you an apology," he says, and Phainon tilts his head quizzically.

"What for?"

"You protected our prince when we were helpless against the witch's curse. As one of his private retinue, this is a grave dishonour." The soldier holds out his free hand. "My name is Hephaestion."

"Phainon." He takes the other man's hand and shakes it. "It's good to meet you."

"You have a good heart, Phainon. I'm sure you don't need me to tell you this, but take care of the prince when we can't?"

Solemnly, he nods. "I will. I swear it on my life."

Hephaestion disappears into the crowd, but Phainon's still approached by a few more Kremnoan soldiers before Mydei comes to find him. One look at him, and they move away from the festivities, heading out into the darkness.

Outside the ring of light that the celebration casts, the gentle veil of night almost seems to muffle all other sounds. Phainon smiles a little when he hears snatches of a drinking song being sung, but he turns his attention to Mydei, who's inspecting one of the houses.

"Mydei. I believe I have something of yours." From around his neck, he takes the braided cord out from under his shirt, revealing the ring of Strife that he'd kept close to him.

"You didn't wear it?" Mydei asks.

"I would've, but farm work isn't kind to jewellery." Phainon undoes the knot with quick fingers, sliding the ring out from the cord. It's warmed by his own body heat, and he holds it out.

Instead of taking it from him, Mydei simply tugs off one of his gauntlets and holds his bare hand out, palm down.

His breath hitches. Carefully, reverently, he slides the ring back onto Mydei's ring finger, and before he can lose his nerve, presses a kiss to the back of his hand. When he looks up, Mydei is already looking at him.

The twin moons of Amphoreus are perfectly aligned tonight, shimmering behind Mydei's head as though the gods themselves acknowledge his worth.

He's not sure who closed the distance between them first, but the force of their kiss is so strong that their teeth knock painfully against each other. It's glorious and perfect and so, so desperate as years of suppressed longing finally burst free. A full body shudder works its way down his spine when he realises that Mydei is just as desperate as he is, and Phainon nips gently at Mydei's bottom lip, who reciprocates by sliding his tongue into Phainon's mouth. His hand grips Mydei's hair, tugging a little too hard to be comfortable, but the other man just growls and crowds closer into his space, pressing him against the wall of the house they're hiding behind.

Eventually, they break apart, even though they remain close enough that their breaths mingle.

"You really…are a beast," Phainon gasps, pushing Mydei away. "Wait, stop, I still need to breathe."

Mydei nips at the hollow of his throat, and Phainon groans, tilting his head back to grant the prince more access. "Perhaps some of the instincts remained."

"Don't you dare blame the curse for this." He pauses, then nuzzles into the crook of Mydei's neck, inhaling the scent of smoked meat and fire. His eyes are hot, and it has nothing to do with the smoke from the cooking fires.

"Phainon."

"I know you had duties, but I waited…" He breaks off into a quiet laugh. "Four years, Mydei. I waited four years for you."

"I know. Every day, I wished we could've done everything faster. But I didn't want to ruin this one chance. If we had, then…" Mydei sighs. "Never mind. There isn't any point in speculating about things that have already come to pass."

"Tell me about them, then. Aedes Elysiae gets no news at all, you know." He laughs, but it's shaky. "I had to beg the bards for news from the outside."

"Why didn't you leave?"

"I considered it," Phainon admits. "But I kept thinking: what if Mydei came back, and he couldn't find me? The thought of waiting endlessly here…it was far better than missing our chance because I was too impatient."

"Never again," Mydei pulls him away, wiping away his tears gently. "If you wish, you can come with us when we leave."

"With you?" Phainon blubbers. "You'd– You'd really–"

"Yes. So dry your tears, Phainon."

"'m not crying. Just…Just the smoke." Phainon sniffles. "You're seeing things."

"Of course." Mydei's smile is small, but heart-achingly fond. "Will you come with me? Will you let me show you everything?"

"Only if you take me to your library. The one you said you forgot."

"Naturally."
